transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling S-Net Customer Accounts. My name is Leah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Leah, my name is Katarzyna. I have just opened my monthly statement for my Fibre 150 broadband and I am shocked—my bill has jumped from £29 a month to £48 a month without warning!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I look at the billing screen, please give me the first line of your postal address and your four-digit security PIN.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, okay—the address is Flat 4, 19 Caledonia Road, Edinburgh, EH11 2DA, and my security PIN is 8420.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That security PIN and address match the account record.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I was saying, I have been paying £29 a month for Fibre 150 for the last two years, and an extra £19 a month out of nowhere is a huge shock to my household budget!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't even have a landline telephone plugged in—I only use the Fibre 150 broadband for working from home—and £48 a month is nearly double what you charge new customers on your website.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your twenty-four-month promotional fixed term ended on the twelfth of last month, so the account automatically rolled onto the standard out-of-contract rack rate of £48 per month.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: £48 per month as a standard rate?! How can a £19 monthly jump overnight be justified when the service hasn't changed at all?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our marketing department sets the out-of-contract pricing, that's nothing to do with me.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, you represent S-Net when I call up! And nobody phoned me or sent a letter through the post to warn me my bill was going up by £19 a month!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, we sent the end-of-contract notification email six weeks ago, if you don't bother reading your emails you can't really blame us.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Excuse me?! That is a really rude way to speak to a loyal customer! Marketing emails often land in the promotions or spam folder, and you don't need to take that condescending tone with me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The system log shows the automated statutory contract-end notice was dispatched on the first of September at 09:14 AM to your registered inbox.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Even so, lecturing me like that is uncalled for. Look, I called today because I cannot afford £48 a month and I want to know if you can put me back onto my £29 loyalty renewal discount.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can open the retention tariff matrix on your profile if you want to enter a new twenty-four-month minimum commitment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I am happy to stay with S-Net for another twenty-four months as long as my price goes back to £29 a month and we sort out this £48 charge that came out today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As for the £48 direct debit that already processed on this month's invoice, billing adjustments for past invoices are handled by the credit control team, not by my desk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why can't you deal with it in one go? First you say out-of-contract pricing has nothing to do with you, and now you say the £19 overcharge on today's bill isn't your job either!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: My desk processes contract re-grades and loyalty tariff renewals going forward. If you want a manual backdated credit on an already issued bill, you have to submit a form to billing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait—if you re-contract my broadband today at £29 a month, doesn't your billing system automatically pro-rate the rest of the current billing period back down to £29?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When a new contract is activated mid-cycle, the billing engine recalculates the advance days from today's date and applies a pro-rata adjustment onto next month's statement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, why didn't you just explain that in the first place instead of telling me to chase another department?! Today is day two of my billing cycle, so a pro-rata adjustment covers almost the whole £19!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, since your cycle runs from the seventeenth to the sixteenth, twenty-nine out of thirty days will recalculate on the next statement once a renewal order completes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine. Let's get the loyalty renewal applied right now then so the rate drops back to £29 a month from today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me open the order builder screen on the CRM.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please make sure nothing else on my setup changes—I just want the exact same broadband speed and router I have now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And which speed tier are you currently on, is it the 150 or the 300?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I literally told you twice at the very start of the call that I am on the Fibre 150 package! Are you even listening to me?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I was looking at the renewal dropdown tab rather than the summary banner. And do you want to keep the Weekend Chatter landline call bundle on the telephone line?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I already told you five minutes ago that I don't even have a landline phone plugged in! I have never had a call bundle—it is broadband only.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, broadband-only Fibre 150 with no voice add-ons.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, broadband-only Fibre 150. What loyalty renewal price comes up on your screen for a twenty-four-month contract?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under the existing-customer retention codes, code RET-F150-29 sets the Fibre 150 monthly rental at £29.00 per month for twenty-four months with zero activation fee.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, £29.00 a month for twenty-four months with zero activation fee—that matches what I was paying before the out-of-contract jump.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me read the mandatory regulatory contract summary before I generate the order. The minimum term is twenty-four months starting today, the eighteenth of October, at £29.00 per month paid by direct debit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I agree to the twenty-four-month term starting today at £29.00 a month.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And each April, the monthly price adjusts in line with the fixed £3.00 annual contract rate set out in the terms sheet, with an early termination fee applying if you cancel inside the twenty-four months.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I have read those standard annual terms before. Please go ahead and process code RET-F150-29 now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I need to push the contract order through the provisioning and billing engine now. Please bear with me while I generate the renewal order on your profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Alright, I will hold while you process it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding. The RET-F150-29 loyalty renewal order has been committed on the billing engine and the new twenty-four-month contract is now live.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that take effect from today immediately, or is there a delay before the billing system updates?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Immediate effect from today's date, and the billing engine has also calculated the mid-cycle pro-rata credit for the period from the eighteenth of October to the sixteenth of November.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How much is the pro-rata credit that it calculated for next month's bill?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has posted an automatic pro-rata credit of £18.37 onto your account ledger, which reduces your November seventeenth direct debit down to £10.63.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, £18.37 credited back so next month's payment is only £10.63, and then £29.00 every month after that—at least the numbers work out properly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The order confirmation number on the system is ORD-774109, and the durable PDF contract summary has been sent to your email inbox.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, let me open my My S-Net app on my phone right now while we are still on the call to make sure it actually shows £29.00 a month and not £48.00.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead and refresh the tariff page in your app.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm pulling down to refresh the My S-Net app... Okay, under 'Current Plan' it now says 'S-Net Fibre 150 Loyalty 24M — £29.00/month', with contract end date October 2028!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And if you tap on the 'Account Balance & Next Bill' tab in the app, you will also see the £18.37 pro-rata credit pending.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me tap on 'Account Balance & Next Bill'... Yes, it shows '-£18.37 Plan Change Adjustment' and estimated next bill £10.63 on the seventeenth of November.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And the durable PDF contract document should also be visible under the 'Documents' tab inside the app.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me check the 'Documents' tab... Yes, the PDF contract for ORD-774109 dated today is right there in the app, so I don't even have to hunt through my email spam folder.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your router will not reboot or lose connection because the physical Fibre 150 line profile remains identical.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, because I am logged into my work VPN all afternoon and didn't want the internet dropping out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No line profile changes were triggered by order ORD-774109, only the commercial tariff code and contract term.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And my direct debit mandate with my bank stays exactly the same—I don't need to re-enter any bank details?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your existing direct debit mandate remains active and will collect £10.63 on the seventeenth of November and £29.00 per month from the seventeenth of December onwards.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, let me double-check the speed tier listed on the PDF summary in the app just to be 100% certain you didn't put me on a slower plan.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Page one of the contract summary lists 'Download Speed: 150 Mbps / Upload Speed: 30 Mbps — Unlimited Data'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I see '150 Mbps download, 30 Mbps upload, £29.00 per month' right here on page one of the PDF.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And page two shows the £0.00 re-contracting fee and the £18.37 pro-rata adjustment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I can see both of those on page two as well.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is the £29.00 loyalty tariff renewal and the £18.37 adjustment for your current bill all confirmed and resolved on your app now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I also check whether there is any paper-bill fee added onto this renewal, because I strictly use digital billing in the app?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Paperless billing is ticked on the account, so the monthly statement charge is £0.00.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what happens in twenty-four months when October 2028 comes around—will it jump by £19 again unless I ring up?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When the twenty-four-month promotional discount expires in October 2028, the discount code drops off automatically unless you renew again in the final thirty days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will put a calendar reminder on my phone for September 2028 right now so I never get caught out by an automatic out-of-contract jump again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can renew through the My S-Net app at any point during the final thirty days of the minimum term.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the new £29.00 contract and the £18.37 credit are both showing live in my app, so the pricing issue itself is resolved.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, everything on order ORD-774109 is completed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I still think your attitude earlier about not reading emails and blaming marketing was pretty poor, even if you did apply the discount in the end.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The loyalty tariff is active on your account now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, well, at least my bill is back to £29 a month. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.
